attributes.body_ja:
「さて」は、話題（わだい）を変（か）えたいときや、新（あたら）しい話題（わだい）に移（うつ）ろうとしているときに使（つか）われる接続詞（せつぞくし）です。

「さて」は、文（ぶん）の始（はじ）まりに置（お）かれます。そして、そのあとに新（あたら）しい話題（わだい）が来（き）ます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「さて」が漢字（かんじ）で書（か）かれることはほとんどありませんが、漢字（かんじ）で書（か）くと「扨（さて）」や「偖（さて）」になります。どちらの漢字（かんじ）も「今（いま）」という意味（いみ）で、新（あたら）しいことを始（はじ）めるときの感（かん）じを表（あらわ）します。
attributes.body:
Acting as a conjunction, さて is a word used when one wants to change the topic of conversation, or is ready to move on to a new point. Usually it is translated as 'well', or 'well then'.

さて will appear at the beginning of a sentence, before the speaker highlights what the new topic is.

Fun Fact

Although さて is extremely rarely written in kanji, 扨（さて） or 偖（さて） may be seen every now and then. Both of these kanji have the same meaning of 'now' (now being the beginning of something new).

attributes.description: Using さて to change the topic

attributes.body: Both mark transitions, but with slightly different nuance. さて is used to shift to a new topic or proceed to the next step, e.g. さて、次の話題に入りましょう ('Now then, let's move on to the next topic.') では・それでは・じゃあ reference the previous context and often lead into a decision or conclusion, similar to 'well then' or 'in that case', e.g. それでは、始めましょう ('Well then, let's begin.')

second_relatable.title: では・それでは・じゃあ
second_relatable.meaning: If so, Well (then), In that case

attributes.body: These are two similar-looking interjections with different uses. さて is a transitional phrase often used at the beginning of sentences to change the topic or move the conversation into a new phase, like 'well then' or 'now then'. In contrast, さ is a casual interjection that serves multiple functions, such as encouragement (e.g. 'all right!', 'come on!') or hesitation ('well, you see...').

second_relatable.title: さ - Interjection
second_relatable.meaning: All right, There we go, Now, You see, Well (I don't know, let me see)
